en.action.label: Reverse proxy
en.audit.description: View recent security events (readable from the local control surface only).
en.audit.label: Audit log
en.check.bootstrapFail: Client trust bootstrap failed — settings may stay memory-scoped.
en.check.bootstrapMissing: No trust bootstrap marker on this page (open via the proxy entry).
en.check.bootstrapOk: Client trust bootstrap is active (isLoopback pinned).
en.check.label: Fence self-check
en.check.proxyStopped: Proxy is stopped: self-check hits the backend only. Start the proxy to verify end-to-end from a phone.
en.check.tlsOff: Local TLS is off (plain HTTP; terminate TLS on the tunnel for public access).
en.check.tokenReadOn: Standing token reads are on (loopback control surface only).
en.check.trustForwardedForOff: X-Forwarded-For trust is off; tunnel clients all appear as 127.0.0.1.
en.check.trustForwardedForOn: X-Forwarded-For trust is enabled (loopback peers only).
en.devices.approvalHint: Approval mode is on: new devices must be approved here before they can connect.
en.devices.empty: No devices yet. Remote browsers appear here after logging in.
en.devices.title: Connected devices
en.error.forbidden: The control request was rejected. Operate this panel from the Harness window on 127.0.0.1 — not from a tunnel or public hostname.
en.error.invalidInviteBase: Invalid invite Origin. Use http(s)://host[:port] with no path.
en.error.invalidListen: Enter a valid listen address and port (0–65535).
en.error.invalidListenServer: Invalid listen address or port. Check the IP/host and port (0–65535), then press Apply listen address.
en.error.invalidRequest: Invalid request. Check your input and retry.
en.error.listenFailed: Cannot listen on {bind}; that port is likely in use. Change to a free port (for example 3081) and apply again, or stop the program holding the port.
en.error.listenRestored: The new address cannot bind (the port is likely in use). Restored {bind}. Pick a free port and apply again.
en.error.loopbackRequired: The control panel can only be used from this computer. Switch back to the local Harness window.
en.error.network: Cannot reach the control API: {detail}. Confirm Harness is still running and open the panel in the local browser.
en.error.notRunning: The proxy is not running, so no invite can be generated. Start the proxy first.
en.error.sessionActionFailed: The device action did not apply (the session may have expired). Refresh the list and retry.
en.error.sessionsPoll: Could not refresh the device list.
en.error.startDisposed: The plugin is shutting down or was unloaded, so it cannot start. Refresh the page or restart DeepSeek Harness.
en.error.startListenFailed: Cannot start the proxy on {bind}; that port is likely in use. Change to a free port (for example 127.0.0.1:3081), press Apply listen address, then Start proxy. Or stop the program holding the port.
en.error.startSelfLoop: Listen address {bind} collides with the Harness backend {backend} and would loop onto itself. Change the port (default 3081), apply it, then start.
en.error.startUnknown: The proxy did not start and no reason was returned. Check that the listen address is free, or read the Harness log.
en.error.tlsFailed: Could not load the TLS certificate or key. Check tlsCertFile / tlsKeyFile and try again.
en.error.tokenReadDisabled: Standing token reads are disabled (allowTokenRead: false). Rotate the token to obtain a new value, or re-enable reads in config.
en.error.unknownReason: The operation did not finish ({reason}). Check the listen address, or read the Harness log.
en.guide.description: Pick the entry by scenario: LAN while at home, your own tunnel on the road. The one-click quick tunnel is for temporary use only.
en.guide.label: Recommended setup
en.guide.outside: On the road: point frp / Tailscale / a named tunnel at the tunnel target below — the plugin works with any tunnel you choose.
en.guide.quick: The one-click quick tunnel gets a random address on every start and is unstable from some networks (notably mainland mobile). Use it for temporary sharing or emergencies only.
en.guide.wifi: At home / same Wi-Fi: open {url} on the phone — fastest and most stable, no public tunnel involved.
en.guide.wifiNone: The proxy is loopback-only right now. To let a phone on the same Wi-Fi connect directly, fill this machine’s LAN IP (e.g. 192.168.x.x) under Listen address.
en.interact.approval.fallback: Tool {tool} needs approval before it can continue.
en.interact.approval.title: Waiting for approval
en.interact.kind.question: Question
en.interact.open.hint: Open the session to choose or approve here.
en.interact.open.title: Action needs confirmation
en.interact.question.unanswered: Choose or type an answer first.
en.invite.description: Build a one-time invite URL and QR (no standing token; single use. Same-IP retries within 60 seconds reuse the original session instead of adding a second device). For a public tunnel, enter that Origin; leave blank to use the tunnel target above.
en.invite.label: Phone invite
en.invite.lanHint: Tunnel off: leaving Origin blank builds a LAN direct invite (recommended at home).
en.invite.requiresRunning: Invites only work while the proxy is running. Start the proxy first.
en.listen.description: IP and port the reverse proxy publishes. Port 0 picks a free port; changing the address restarts a running proxy automatically.
en.listen.label: Listen address
en.listen.warn: Binding a non-loopback address exposes the port directly; make sure your firewall and tunnel are configured correctly.
en.listen.wildcard: 0.0.0.0 / :: bind every interface but are not connectable destinations. For phone-on-WiFi, fill a concrete LAN IP. The copyable target below is a reachable address.
en.section.intro: Publish a token-gated local entry point. Point any tunnel at the address below to use DeepSeek Harness remotely.
en.section.title: Reverse proxy
en.status.loadingHint: Reading proxy status from the local control surface.
en.status.runningHint: You can now point any tunnel at the local endpoint below.
en.status.stoppedHint: Starting it creates a token-protected local entry point.
en.toast.started: Proxy is running. Point your tunnel’s local target at the address below.
en.toast.tokenRotated: Access token rotated. Existing remote sessions are now invalid. Generate a new phone invite.
en.toast.tokenRotatedWithIssue: Access token rotated and sessions cleared, but the proxy did not restart cleanly: {detail}
en.token.description: Remote browsers must enter this token on first visit. Rotating it invalidates existing remote sessions.
en.token.label: Access token
en.tunnel.bound: Currently bound to {bind} (wildcard; not directly connectable)
en.tunnel.description: Point your frp, ngrok, cloudflared, or SSH tunnel at:
en.tunnel.errorConfiguredPathInvalid: The cloudflaredPath file is not executable. Check the config.
en.tunnel.errorConnectFailed: The tunnel failed to establish. Retry.
en.tunnel.errorConnectTimeout: The tunnel timed out (45 s). Check the network and retry.
en.tunnel.errorDownloadFailed: cloudflared download failed. Check the network and retry.
en.tunnel.errorExited: The tunnel exited unexpectedly. Start it again.
en.tunnel.errorIntegrityFailed: The cloudflared download failed its checksum and was discarded. Retry, or install it yourself and set cloudflaredPath.
en.tunnel.errorSpawnFailed: The cloudflared process could not start. Check that the binary works.
en.tunnel.errorTlsUnsupported: Local TLS is enabled, which cannot be combined with the quick tunnel (the Cloudflare edge already provides HTTPS). Disable tlsCertFile / tlsKeyFile and retry.
en.tunnel.errorUnsupportedPlatform: There is no official cloudflared build for this platform (for example Windows ARM64). Install it yourself and set cloudflaredPath.
en.tunnel.hint.ephemeral: The address is random: stopping and restarting produces a new one, and old invite links and logins stop working.
en.tunnel.hint.inviteUsesTunnel: Tunnel online: phone invites will use the tunnel address (the Origin above can still override it).
en.tunnel.hint.requiresProxy: Start the proxy first — the tunnel needs a listener to forward to.
en.tunnel.hint.tlsBlocked: Local TLS is on, which cannot be combined with the quick tunnel (the Cloudflare edge already provides HTTPS).
en.tunnel.label: Tunnel target
en.tunnel.oneClick.description: Start a Cloudflare quick tunnel on this machine (free, no account) and get a random https://…trycloudflare.com address. The address changes on every start, so it suits temporary sharing; for a stable daily entry use your own frp / ngrok / named tunnel.
en.tunnel.oneClick.label: One-click public tunnel
en.tunnel.state.downloading: First use downloads cloudflared (18–52 MB), please wait…
en.tunnel.target.recommended: Recommended: with the phone on the same Wi-Fi, open the address above directly (LAN, fastest).
